about.apiSteamHint: Avatar in title bar · mod update checks
about.heroTagline: Server browser & mod manager for DayZ Standalone
about.infoCopied: Copied: paste it into your bug report.
about.modDownloaderTip: Mods download through SteamCMD or the Steam client: switch between them from the status bar, at the bottom of the window.
about.modStep1: Connect to a server — the app offers to install any missing mods automatically.
about.modStep2: Go to the Mods tab and click Check updates to see which mods are outdated.
about.modStep3: Click Update N to update all stale mods in one batch, or update them individually.
about.offStep1: Open the Offline tab and install DayZCommunityOfflineMode in one click; it updates the same way.
about.offStep2: Pick a mission by map: the launcher lists those of the mode and your own.
about.offStep3: Launch it: DayZ starts alone, without a server, with the mods the mission needs.
about.profileExportDesc: Save settings, favorites, history to a {file} file (zstd-compressed, portable between machines).
about.profileImportDesc: Restore a previously exported {file} file. Overwrites current profile and mod list.
about.profileResetDesc: Wipe profile back to factory defaults — clears all settings, favorites, history and launch options. Installed mods on disk are not affected.
about.qsStep1Body: Click your name (or "Set up account") in the title bar to configure your player name, Steam credentials, and API keys.
about.qsStep2Body: This is the character name passed as -name= when launching DayZ.
about.qsStep3Body: Use the Servers tab to find a server. Double-click a row or click Connect to launch DayZ directly.
about.sharingDcStep1: Query a server in the Direct Connect tab (or press D on a server in the list).
about.sharingDcStep2: Click Copy URL to copy a dzch:// link to the clipboard, or Export .dzch to save a file.
about.sharingDcStep3: Send the link or file to friends — they open it and the app handles the rest.
about.sharingDesc: Share a server with friends by copying a {url} URL or exporting a {file} file from the Direct Connect tab. When someone opens the link or file, the app automatically fills in the server address, queries for live info, and offers to install any missing mods before connecting.
about.sharingFilesDesc: A small JSON file containing the full server config including mod names. Double-click one to open it in the app, or use the {button} button in the Direct Connect tab to create one.
about.sharingParamQport: Query port for A2S (falls back to heuristics if omitted)
about.srcLiveDesc: Players, rules and mods, asked of each server (A2S)
about.srcModsDesc: Steam Workshop, through SteamCMD or the Steam client
about.srcOfficialDesc: Steam's master server, with a Steam API key
about.srcServersDesc: The public list of DayZ SA Launcher
about.srcStatsDesc: Rank, uptime, schedules and history from DayZ Metrics
about.steamcmdDesc: A command-line tool from Valve used to download Steam Workshop content without the full Steam client. The app uses it to install and update DayZ mods in the background. If the title bar shows {notFound}, install it below or set the path manually in account settings.
about.steamcmdWinDesc: SteamCMD will be downloaded from Valve and installed to
about.systemHint: Used to suggest -cpuCount, -exThreads and -maxMem in Launch options.
about.tipAuthStep3: Return to rename menu and rename back, apply
about.tipPerfDesc: The launcher may be slower while the progress bar on the Servers tab is visible (pinging servers in background).
about.updatesDevBuild: This is a development build: updates are not installed from here.
about.updatesDoneHint: The installer is launching — the app will restart automatically.
about.updatesPackageManager: On this system, updates come through your package manager or a new release download.

settings.steamcmdExplain: SteamCMD downloads into the launcher's own folder with its own login. Your Steam account and libraries are left alone. Steam allows one session per account on a computer: each SteamCMD login disconnects the Steam client, which you then put back online.
settings.steamcmdInstallLinux: Install it with your package manager:
settings.steamcmdMissing: Not found: mods cannot be downloaded
settings.steamcmdOnDeckMessage: On a Steam Deck the Steam client downloads mods itself, in Game Mode too. SteamCMD needs its own login and Steam Guard code, and downloads beside Steam. Switch anyway?

settings.steamcmdPathHint: Leave empty to use the one found on this machine.
settings.steamworksExplain: Like the DZSA launcher, the Steam client downloads: Steam must be running and logged in. Each mod is subscribed on your Steam account, lands in your own Steam library (steamapps/workshop/content/221100), and Steam keeps it updated from then on. While mods download, Steam shows you as playing DayZ.
settings.steamworksTestOk: Steam answered: mods will download through it.

settings.usernameHint: Leave empty to download mods anonymously where possible.
settings.windowHint: How the frameless window is drawn. Rounded corners need a compositor that supports them.
settings.yourThemeHint: Twelve colours; every border, tint and muted text is worked out from them.

setup.doneDesc: Click {button} to save your profile and start browsing servers.
setup.doneSettingsHint: You can update any of these settings later by clicking your name in the title bar.
setup.downloadsDesc: Both install the mods a server needs before you join. You can switch at any time from the status bar.
setup.filledFromSteam: Filled in from your running Steam client, with your Steam id. Change it if you play under another name.
setup.gameDesc: The launcher looks in every Steam library, on every drive. Pick the library yourself if DayZ is somewhere else.
setup.gameLibraryHint: The folder that holds steamapps, on any drive. Leave empty to search on its own.
setup.gameNotFoundHint: Install DayZ from Steam, or pick the Steam library that holds it. You can carry on without it and set it later in Settings.
setup.importHint: Coming from another computer? Bring its favourites, history and settings with a profile file.
setup.loginNotNeeded: Mods download through the Steam client: no Steam login is needed here.
setup.loginOnce: Your password is never saved. SteamCMD asks for it and for Steam Guard at the first download, then remembers the login on this computer.
setup.servicesDesc: Both are optional and can be added later in Settings.
setup.steamApiDesc: Enables avatar display and higher rate limits for mod update checks. You can add these later.
setup.steamClosed: Steam is not running. Start it before you download mods.
setup.steamOk: Steam is running: mods will download through it.
setup.steamRequired: Steam username is required for SteamCMD to download and update mods.
setup.steamcmdLinuxHint: Install SteamCMD with your package manager:
setup.steamcmdLinuxWaiting: Waiting for SteamCMD to be installed…
setup.steamcmdWinHint: You can install SteamCMD automatically or point to an existing installation.
setup.welcomeFeat2: Manage and update your mods via SteamCMD
setup.welcomeFeat4: Launch DayZ directly with one click
setup.welcomeHint: This quick setup takes about 1 minute. You can change everything later in Settings.
setup.welcomeSubtitle: A server browser and mod manager for DayZ Standalone

shell.noHistory: No history entry to reconnect to
shell.notifyUpdateBody: DayZ Community Hub {version} is ready to install.
shell.sbBeDisabled: BattlEye's service is disabled in Windows: nothing can start it, and BattlEye servers will kick DayZ.
shell.sbBeInstallAction: Click to have Steam install it.
shell.sbBeInstalling: Steam is installing the Proton BattlEye Runtime.
shell.sbBeMissing: BattlEye's service is not installed, or its program was removed: BattlEye servers will kick DayZ.
shell.sbBeMissingProton: The Proton BattlEye Runtime is not installed: BattlEye servers will kick DayZ.
shell.sbBeNotStarted: DayZ is running without BattlEye: its service did not start, so BattlEye servers will kick it. Close DayZ and join again from here.
shell.sbBeReady: BattlEye is installed: its service starts with DayZ.
shell.sbBeReadyProton: The Proton BattlEye Runtime is installed, so BattlEye servers accept DayZ. Under Proton, BattlEye starting with the game cannot be seen from here.
shell.sbBeRepairAction: Click to reinstall it (administrator rights are asked).
shell.sbBeRepairing: Repairing BattlEye: accept the administrator prompt.
shell.sbBeStillMissing: BattlEye is still not ready. Run BattlEye\Install_BattlEye.bat in the DayZ folder as administrator.
shell.sbFetchingTip: Fetching the launcher list and Steam's official servers; the current list stays usable meanwhile.
shell.sbGameQuit: If it hangs, close it from the foot of the menu.
shell.sbListFailedTip: The last fetch failed: {error}. Click to try again.
shell.sbListStaleTip: The list was fetched {age}: servers may have come and gone since. Click to fetch it again.
shell.sbListTip: {count} servers in the list, fetched {age}. Click to fetch it again.
shell.sbModOpTip: {kind} with {via}: {name}, {current} of {total}. Click to show the progress.
shell.sbModWaitingTip: SteamCMD is waiting for your Steam Guard confirmation or password. Click to answer.
shell.sbModsBehindTip: {count} installed mods have a newer version on the Workshop. Click to open Mods.
shell.sbModsCheckingTip: Asking the Workshop which installed mods have a newer version.
shell.sbOfflineTip: Installing the offline mode in the background. Click to open Offline mode.
shell.sbPingPausedTip: The ping scan is paused at {done} of {total}; resume it here.
shell.sbPingTip: Pinging every server for its latency: {done} of {total}. The list sorts by ping as they answer.
shell.sbSteamAction: Click to switch or open the Steam settings.
shell.sbSteamClient: Mods download through the Steam client.
shell.sbSteamCmdAs: Mods download with SteamCMD, signed in as {login}.
shell.sbSteamCmdNoLogin: Mods download with SteamCMD, not signed in yet.
shell.sbSteamDown: Steam is not running: DayZ cannot start, and downloads through Steam wait for it.
shell.sbSteamListingTip: Listing community servers from Steam: {done} of {total} requests, {added} servers added so far. Click to see the list's sources.
shell.sbSteamcmdMissingTip: Mods cannot download until SteamCMD is installed or the Steam client is chosen to download them. Click to open the Steam settings.
shell.sbUpdateElsewhereTip: Version {version} of the launcher is out. Click to see what changed: this copy is updated outside the launcher.
shell.sbUpdateReadyTip: The new version is in place. Click to restart from About.
shell.sbUpdateTip: Version {version} of the launcher is out. Click to see what changed and install it.
shell.sbUpdatingTip: Downloading launcher v{version}: {percent}%. Click to follow it in About.
shell.titlebarPlayersIngame: Players on those servers right now
shell.titlebarPlayersSteam: Players in DayZ on Steam right now

sources.duplicatesHint: Entries that lead to the same server (same address to join): each was asked, and only the one answering for that address stays.
sources.dzsaHint: dayzsalauncher.com: the community servers, with their mods.
sources.keptHint: Servers earlier lists had and the new one lacks: kept while they answer.
sources.remembered: Known fakes, silent or duplicates (not asked again yet)
sources.steamHint: Every server Steam's master lists, through the Steam Web API (a key in Settings › API keys; split past Steam's 10 000 cap). Each new address is queried, farms left out.
sources.title: Where the list comes from
sources.waiting: Steam is rationing requests: next in {secs} s

stats.activityHint: Time played each day over the last year, in your time. Darker is longer.
stats.emptyHint: Join a server or an offline map: the launcher writes down how long DayZ runs, where and when.
stats.exportHint: Your play history is part of the profile: exporting it keeps these stats, importing brings them back.
stats.historySearch: Search a server, an address, a map…
stats.pickHint: Choose a day, a server or a map to list its sessions below.
stats.streakTitle: Days in a row with play, ending today. Best: {best}.
stats.unmeasuredHint: A join from before the launcher measured play time: it happened, its length is not known.
stats.whenHint: Time played by weekday and hour, in your time.

theme.blurbChernarus: The launcher's own: khaki ground, amber accent.
theme.blurbChristmas: Cold night blue, Christmas red, falling snow.
theme.blurbForest: Deep pine green with moss and lichen.
theme.blurbGithubDark: GitHub's dark theme: blue-black and GitHub blue.
theme.blurbGithubLight: GitHub's light theme: white, cool grey and GitHub blue.

theme.blurbGruvboxLight: Gruvbox on cream paper, earthy marks.
theme.blurbHalloween: Purple night, pumpkin orange, slime green.
theme.blurbMilitary: Olive drab and coyote tan, low glare.
theme.blurbNord: Arctic slate and frost, soft contrast.
theme.blurbOled: Pure black and the house amber, for OLED screens and night play.
theme.blurbPowder: Fresh snow by day, holly red.
theme.blurbTokyonight: Cold night blue with neon marks.
theme.blurbTopo: The launcher's own in daylight: survey-map paper, olive ink.
theme.deriveHint: Keeps the floor and the accent, and works out the other ten colours so every check passes.
theme.followSystemHint: Wears one theme when the desktop is dark and another when it is light.
theme.legibilityHint: WCAG contrast ratio of each pair, beside the minimum it needs; pairs below it are flagged.
theme.name: Name
theme.resetHint: Back to the colours it was duplicated from
theme.yourThemesEmpty: None yet: duplicate any theme to make it yours.
